items.claim: The span is defensible, but its front seam rests on topic alone with no person shift disclosed, the tested alternative it offers is not a realizable contiguous span, and its note on the divine-name site before the span places that site wrongly.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: the verse-initial letters of Lam.4.12-Lam.4.16 are lamed, mem, nun, samekh and pe at pinned positions twelve through sixteen of this poem's pe-before-ayin order, exactly as stated, and that order is correctly not called the standard one; the samekh marks at Lam.4.11-Lam.4.16 are correct and never conflated with pe; the ketiv/qere notes in the span do stand at Lam.4.12 and Lam.4.16 and nowhere else in it; the divine-name site census is right (the name stands at Lam.4.11, Lam.4.16 and Lam.4.20 in this poem - sweep: 3 verses in the chapter, 32 verses book-wide). Defect 1 - the seam is topical only and is not disclosed as such. Across Lam.4.11-Lam.4.16 every finite verb and every pronominal suffix reads third person (byte-read of all six verses; sweep: 0 verses in that window carrying a first-plural-suffix token or a first-plural pronoun); the two plural-ending tokens the suffix test raises there, הֶאֱמִ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the all-term, not at this run) and חָנָֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the elders-term, not at this run), are third-plural perfects. The unit is bounded by neither a voice nor an addressee change, and the only other evidence carried is the parashah layer, which cannot discriminate any seam inside this poem: every one of Lam.4.1-Lam.4.21 carries a samekh and Lam.4.22 the pe (sweep: 21 samekh and 1 pe over the poem's 22 verses; book-wide 84 samekh and 5 pe over 89 marked verses, the pe sites being Lam.1.22, Lam.2.22, Lam.3.66, Lam.4.22 and Lam.5.18). Defect 2 - the tested alternative is unrealizable. It proposes ending at Lam.4.14 while keeping Lam.4.15 with the nobles' fall in the earlier verses; the nobles-term stands only at Lam.4.7, נְזִירֶ֨יהָ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.7, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse book-wide), outside this span, so no contiguous span answers the description and the field carries no alternative that could actually be weighed. Defect 3 - the divine-name note says the mention at Lam.4.11 opened the unit standing before this one. Lam.4.11 is the verse immediately preceding this span, so under an exact tiling it stands at that unit's close rather than at its opening; the site is right and its position is not.

items.claim: The seam taken is the byte-correct one, but the case made for it is not: the tested alternative is called the more probable seam on a ground that refutes it, the first-plural onset claim ships without its digit, and the closing verse is retitled past its own bytes.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: Lam.4.17 opens with its ketiv/qere pair, the qere עוֹדֵ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.17, byte tier), on the ayin line at pinned position seventeen of the pe-before-ayin order, with tsade, qof and resh following at eighteen through twenty as stated; the samekh disclosure runs complete from Lam.4.16 through Lam.4.20; the held-open posture, the low-side confidence and the frontier flag match a genuinely contested onset; the unit-label deviation is disclosed as required. Defect 1 - the onset claim is byte-true but undigited. No first-plural-suffix token and no first-plural pronoun stands anywhere in Lam.4.1-Lam.4.16 (sweep: 0 verses; the two plural-ending tokens there are third-plural perfects), while Lam.4.17-Lam.4.20 carry fifteen first-plural-suffix tokens over four consecutive verses (5, 5, 3 and 2 respectively). The claim that the plural enters at the ayin line is the strongest evidence in the row and is the one claim left without a count. Defect 2 - the tested alternative is self-refuting. It names Lam.4.16 as the more probable seam and grounds that on the verse's forms staying third person about them rather than us. The only plural-looking form there is חָנָֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the elders-term, not at this run), whose ending is the third-plural perfect of a geminate root, and the row's own rendering of that clause makes its subject third person. Nothing at Lam.4.16 supplies a first-plural onset, so the stated ground is in fact the strongest argument for the seam actually taken, and the field as written asserts the opposite. Defect 3 - calling Lam.4.20 the king's capture goes past the bytes. מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Lam.4.20, byte tier) is the book's only anointed-term (sweep: 1 verse book-wide), and the one king-term in this poem, מַלְכֵי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the all-term, not at this run), denotes the nations' kings.

items.claim: The span, its address evidence and its flagged concern all hold, but the cohesion ground given for keeping the two verses together names shared vocabulary that stands in one verse apiece, and the genre label ascribes to the unit a speech class the book nowhere carries.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: the two-token address to Edom stands in both verses (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside this span) and the daughter-of-Zion formula at Lam.4.22 is one of eight (sweep: 8 verses book-wide); both splices reach byte tier; shin and tav at pinned positions twenty-one and twenty-two close the poem; the samekh at Lam.4.20 and Lam.4.21 and the pe at Lam.4.22 are correct and unconflated. The flagged concern on this row is confirmed as a false positive: the variant at Lam.4.21 attaches to the dwelling-participle, not to the spliced address, and the note is disclosed in the row - it sits outside the field carrying the splice, which is a placement matter and not a missing disclosure. Defect 1 - the cohesion ground fails at the bytes. The cup-term כּ֔וֹס (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the dwelling-participle, not at this run) stands in Lam.4.21 only (sweep: 1 verse book-wide), and the iniquity-term עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.22, byte tier) stands in Lam.4.22 only within this span (sweep: 4 verses book-wide - Lam.2.14, Lam.4.13, Lam.4.22, Lam.5.7). Neither term is shared across the two verses, so the shared cup and iniquity vocabulary offered as the reason for one span does not exist; the item genuinely shared is the address formula the row's own device note already names. Defect 2 - the genre label calls the unit an oracle against Edom, which ascribes prophetic divine speech to a span that carries none. Lam.4.21 runs on second-feminine-singular imperatives and imperfects in the poet's own voice and Lam.4.22 on third-masculine-singular verbs with second-feminine-singular suffixes; no first-person divine voice, no messenger formula and no speech-event stands anywhere in this book. Defect 3 - the substrate-signal list carries a key naming the poem-closing parashah mark; that layer is weak single-witness corroboration belonging to prose disclosure, not to the signal list.

items.claim: The poem-onset evidence is sound, but the closing seam cuts a byte-marked four-verse block after its first member with no weighing from either side, and both petition-imperative digits misname what they count.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: the poem opens with its remember-imperative and the divine name at byte tier; the ketiv/qere pair in the same verse reaches byte tier and is disclosed in-field, and the further notes at Lam.5.3, Lam.5.5 and doubled Lam.5.7 are disclosed and complete for the span; this chapter carries no acrostic letter, as stated; the pe at Lam.4.22 stands immediately before the span and is correctly weighted; the divine name stands nowhere in Lam.5.2-Lam.5.11 (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter - Lam.5.1, Lam.5.19, Lam.5.21). Defect 1 - the closing seam is unargued and the bytes contest it. Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14 form a marked block on two independent tests: each of the four opens with a bare plural social-group noun - נָשִׁים֙, שָׂרִים֙, בַּחוּרִים֙, זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.11, oshb:Lam.5.12, oshb:Lam.5.13, oshb:Lam.5.14, all byte tier) - and they are the only run in Lam.5.1-Lam.5.18 carrying no first-plural form at all (sweep: every verse of Lam.5.1-Lam.5.10 and of Lam.5.15-Lam.5.17 carries at least one first-plural-suffix token; those 4 verses carry none, the single plural-ending token at Lam.5.11 being a third-plural verb, and a byte-read of the four confirms every finite verb there is third-plural). The unit ends after that block's first member; the block's own onset is at Lam.5.11, and nothing in the row weighs the seam from either side. Defect 2 - both cited censuses misname their object. Given as three verses book-wide for a petition imperative, the remember-census includes the negated third-masculine-singular perfect זָכַ֥ר (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier), leaving two imperative sites (Lam.3.19 and this poem's onset). Given as two verses book-wide, the look-census is a bare-token count that drops the two clearest petition onsets to the divine name, וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה at Lam.1.11 (oshb:Lam.1.11, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the pleasant-things term, not at this run) and the byte-identical run at Lam.2.20 (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier; collated against both verses), both standing behind the single-letter prefix this book's own tolerance test admits; under that test the form stands in 4 verses (Lam.1.11, Lam.2.20, Lam.3.63, Lam.5.1). Defect 3 - the onset is called a doubled imperative, but the verse carries three, the third being וּרְאֵ֥ה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the look-imperative, which the row splices and discloses), itself one of the book's censused petition onsets (sweep: 7 verses book-wide under the single-letter prefix test, 6 as a bare token - this verse's own occurrence carries the prefix).

items.claim: The front seam opens inside a byte-marked block and the row concedes the continuity in its first sentence without weighing it, the closing parashah mark is used as an argument rather than as weak corroboration, and two substrate-signal keys have no byte object.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: both splices reach byte tier; this chapter's only parashah mark is the pe at Lam.5.18 and it is correctly not conflated with samekh; the ketiv/qere and paseq inventories are indeed empty across Lam.5.12-Lam.5.17, and across Lam.5.18 as well; the sin-verb at Lam.5.16 is the span's only one (sweep: 7 verses book-wide for that root, 1 inside this span). Defect 1 - the front seam. The row's own opening states that the catalogue continues across it, and the bytes agree: Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14 open alike with a bare plural social-group noun - נָשִׁים֙, שָׂרִים֙, בַּחוּרִים֙, זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.11, oshb:Lam.5.12, oshb:Lam.5.13, oshb:Lam.5.14, all byte tier) - and are the only run in Lam.5.1-Lam.5.18 with no first-plural form (sweep: 0 first-plural-suffix tokens across those 4 verses, whose finite verbs all read third-plural on a byte-read; at least one such token in every verse of Lam.5.1-Lam.5.10 and Lam.5.15-Lam.5.17). A device true at the bytes straddles this unit's own seam undisclosed, and the block's onset stands one verse earlier than the seam taken. Defect 2 - the tested alternative is settled partly on the ground that the mark at Lam.5.18 argues for keeping that verse inside the unit. That layer is weak single-witness corroboration in this canon division; it may corroborate a close already carried by the text signals, but it cannot itself argue a seam against a competing reading. Defect 3 - two substrate-signal keys fail at the bytes. One names the closing parashah mark, which belongs to prose disclosure rather than the signal list, and in the same key calls Lam.5.18 hymnic when the hymnic turn stands at Lam.5.19 with אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.19, byte tier). The other claims personification at Lam.5.18, where הַר צִיּוֹן֙ is resumed by the third-masculine-singular בֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.5.18, byte tier) as a place, and no daughter-formula of any kind stands anywhere in this chapter (sweep: 0 verses in the chapter across all six formulas, whose book-wide totals are 8, 5, 3, 2, 2 and 2 verses). Defect 4 - the sin-confession is placed at the span's centre; the span runs seven verses and Lam.5.16 is its fifth.

items.claim: The row is byte-clean on every seam, quotation, census and disclosure test in its span; one closing description misplaces the petition it says is framed and miscounts the span.
items.evidence: Confirmed first: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.19, byte tier) opens the span and reopens the divine name after the descriptive verses behind it, which carry none (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter - Lam.5.1, Lam.5.19, Lam.5.21 - and none across Lam.5.2-Lam.5.18); the closing ketiv/qere pair reaches byte tier with its note disclosed in-field; the paseq citation is right, count-only and single-witness (1 site across these two poems, at Lam.5.21); the pe at Lam.5.18 stands immediately before the span and is weighted as weak corroboration rather than as a driver; the whole-poem reading is set aside explicitly as a chapter-fallback, with the held-open posture, the low-side confidence and the frontier flag all carried honestly; this chapter carries no acrostic and none is claimed. The one defect: the closing note calls Lam.5.21 this unit's centre and says the two divine-name sites frame the petition between them. The span runs four verses, so Lam.5.21 is its third; and the verse standing between the two name-sites, Lam.5.20, carries second-masculine-singular imperfects with first-plural object suffixes in a why-question, תִּשְׁכָּחֵ֔נוּ (oshb:Lam.5.20, byte tier), while the span's only petition imperative is הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ (oshb:Lam.5.21, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the return-verb, which the row splices and discloses). The framed verse is not the petition and the petition is one of the frames. Nothing else in the span is contested by the bytes.
